reason: R8H-1 rests on the assumption that 'public = one embryo'. That is a participants' guess, not a host fact. The hosts say the test holds two embryos and that public is ~29% of the test data (research/discussions_summary.md l.4-6; browser_intel.md l.210). How the host split rows between public and private is unknown. If the split is by video, both prefixes hold public and private clips. Then branch (i), 'S only -> STOP, no private value', would kill the line in exactly the case where the splice touches the ~71% private share of that embryo, and the S/L bits would pick the wrong tie rule. The downside is lopsided: stopping on a false read loses private gain, while continuing when S really is public-only costs one slot and leaves private unchanged. The decision value is also small. L-only maps to tie rule T1 (adopt at 0.954), which is the same action as the current G-LB (>= 0.954). The second bit changes the action only in the S-only case and in an exact 0.954 tie with S=L=1. Feasibility: G-A has already FAILED as written (PC8-01: 43/62, or 58/62 counting pairs rejected at the right offset; precision is perfect). The pre-registered default is STOP, and CONTEXT holds no post-hoc user decision as of 10:37Z. Building a more complex probe (per-prefix grouping, a 4 h sleep, a malformed CSV, tests, a local run on >10 clips, a NEW OK and a CONTEXT table) before that decision is premature. It also pushes the slow-branch answer to ~17-18Z. The latency separation itself works: <= 0.8 h vs >= 4 h, read by the 10-min poller. The timing side channel on the hidden set goes further than the approved 1-bit error probe. The rules are silent on it (08:49Z check), so this is a spirit risk, not a rule breach.
fix: Adopt only PC8-02's crash separation in the same approved slot. An accepted pair gives a deliberately malformed CSV ('Scoring/Format Error'). No pair gives the valid minimal CSV. An outer try around both cells maps any unintended exception to 'no CSV'. Threw Exception, a timeout or a Kaggle Error means UNKNOWN: stop and ask. Write the class -> meaning table in CONTEXT before the submit. Drop the S/L decision branches and the 4 h sleep. Print the per-prefix pair counts in the summary log as info only. Submit only after the user's logged post-hoc decision on the failed G-A. If K6 is later adopted at a 0.954 tie under G-LB, CONTEXT must state that the adoption rests on the in-sample G-B alone (R8H-2 T3), whatever the embryo split is.
realistic_gain: 0 score. As proposed, the second bit carries negative expected value: its STOP branch can drop a private gain of up to ~+0.001..0.002 (0.71 x +0.002..0.003 on a 44b6-type embryo) when public and private are split by video. The kept part (crash separation) removes the false 'overlap' read that would waste one slot and a 7.5 h K6 run.
